usageNotes: Releases the cluster-wide SDN configuration lock, which is acquired before applying SDN changes and must be released when done or when a previous apply operation left the lock stuck. Normally supply the `lock-token` returned when the lock was acquired; use `force: true` only to break a stale lock when the original token is unavailable, as forcing bypasses the token check and can discard in-progress changes made by another session. Requires `SDN.Allocate` on `/sdn`.

examples.summary: Release an SDN lock using the token acquired earlier

destructiveReason: Force-releasing the lock without the original token can silently discard uncommitted SDN configuration changes that another session was in the process of applying.
tips: The lock token is returned by the corresponding lock-acquire call (POST /cluster/sdn/lock); store it immediately before making SDN changes.
Use `force: true` only as a last resort for stuck locks — confirm no other apply is actively running first.
This call returns null on success; any non-null error response means the lock was not released.
After releasing the lock, verify the SDN state with GET /cluster/sdn to confirm the expected configuration is active.
